successors.name: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)
successors.text: Wallachia as drawn in its last Cliopatria shape (1857-1858): Muntenia and Oltenia

ledger.x: c. 1310: Basarab I begins his reign in Wallachia. The page dates the reign 'c. 1310' or 'between 1304 and 1324'; the first document naming him is a charter of 26 July 1324 that shows him 'subject to Charles I of Hungary as the voivode of Wallachia'. The Wallachia page's infobox adds a legendary 'Dismounting by Radu…
1325: Basarab I seizes the Banate of Severin.
1330: Charles I of Hungary marches into Wallachia.
1330: Wallachian independence at Posada.

c. 1400: Mircea the Elder reaches the Danube Delta. The page says Mircea 'briefly extended rule to the Danube Delta, Dobruja and Silistra (c. 1400–1404)'; it does not name the previous holder (Cliopatria's Despotate of Dobruja ends in 1394, so the Ottomans are taken as counterpart). The Mircea I page has Dobruja…

c. 1404: Mircea's hold on Dobruja ends. The same sentence closes the span at 1404 ('c. 1400–1404'). The Mircea I page says 'In 1404 Mircea was thus able to impose his rule on Dobruja again', which conflicts with a loss in 1404; the Wallachia page's span is followed.
1418: the court settles at Târgoviște, a year after Wallachia 'accepted a peace treaty with the Ottomans in 1417' (infobox: Ottoman vassal 1417-1862).
1594: Michael the Brave storms the Ottoman Danube forts.
October 1599: Michael the Brave takes Transylvania.
May 1600: Michael the Brave enters Moldavia.
1600: Michael loses Transylvania.
1600: Michael loses Moldavia.
1600: Polish troops split Wallachia.
1601: Simion Movilă is driven out.
1601: the Danube forts of 1594 are back with the Ottomans.
1659: the capital moves to Bucharest (infobox: Bucharest from 1659).
1716: Austrian troops hold Oltenia.
1718: the occupation becomes annexation (see the loss below).
1718: Oltenia goes to the Habsburgs.
18 September 1739: Oltenia is returned.
17 November 1769: Russia occupies Bucharest.
1774: Russia returns Wallachia.
1789: 'Habsburg troops, under Prince Josias of Coburg, again entered the country during the Russo-Turkish-Austrian War, deposing Nicholas Mavrogenes in 1789.'
4 August 1791: the Treaty of Sistova; 'Austria returned all the territory from its conquests save the small town of Orsova', so the occupation of Wallachia ends.
1806: Russia reoccupies Wallachia.
28 May 1812: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the occupation.
April-May 1828: 'In April and May 1828, the Russian commander-in-chief, Prince Peter Wittgenstein, moved into the Danubian Principalities.'
14 September 1829: the Danube forts come to Wallachia.
1 April 1834: the Russian occupation ends.

27 September 1848: 'a Russian force under Alexander von Lüders joined the occupation of Bucharest, taking over administration over one half of the city', after the revolution of June 1848 was put down.
25 September 1848 (13 September O.S.): 'Ottoman troops headed by Omar Pasha and assisted by Fuat Pasha stormed into Bucharest'.
April 1851: the Russian occupation ends.
April 1851: the Ottoman troops leave with the Russians (Regulamentul Organic page: the occupations 'both lasted until April 1851').
July 1853: 'The Danube campaign opened when the Russians occupied the Danubian Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia in July 1853.'
Late July 1854: 'The Russians evacuated Wallachia and Moldavia in late July 1854' (on 26 July Nicholas I, answering an Austrian ultimatum, ordered the withdrawal).
1854: Austria administers Wallachia.
1856: the Austrian administration ends with the Treaty of Paris (the page pairs the Treaty of Paris with the 1854-1856 administration).
5 February 1859: Wallachia unites with Moldavia.
1859: Wallachia ends in the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia, 'of Romania from 1862'.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

wars.name: Battle of Posada
wars.outcome: Wallachian victory: Charles I's royal troops were ambushed between 9 and 12 November 1330; Hungarian suzerainty ended and Wallachia became independent.

wars.name: Mircea I's war with Bayezid I (Battle of Rovine)
wars.outcome: No border moved on the pages opened: the Battle of Rovine (17 May 1395) is 'Disputed' in its infobox, and the page says that 'the Ottoman Empire was not able to conquer Wallachia at this time'.

wars.name: Vlad III's war with Mehmed II (Night Attack at Târgoviște)
wars.outcome: No border moved on the pages opened: Mehmed II crossed the Danube at Nikopol on 4 June 1462, Vlad's Night Attack of 16-17 June failed to capture him, Mehmed entered Târgoviște at the end of June and left; Vlad was replaced by his brother Radu III in July 1462…

wars.name: Michael the Brave's campaigns
wars.outcome: Michael took the Danube forts (1594), beat Sinan Pasha at Călugăreni (13 August 1595), won Transylvania (Șelimbăr, 18 October 1599) and Moldavia (May 1600), lost both and Wallachia to Hungarian nobles and Poland in 1600 and was killed on 9 August 1601.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1716-1718
wars.outcome: Habsburg victory: by the Treaty of Passarowitz the Ottomans conceded Oltenia to Charles VI, who annexed it as the Banat of Craiova.

wars.name: Austro-Russian-Turkish War of 1735-1739
wars.outcome: The Habsburgs ceded the Banat of Craiova (Oltenia) and Belgrade to the Ottomans at the Treaty of Belgrade (18 September 1739); Oltenia returned to Wallachia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Russia occupied Moldavia (Iași, 7 October 1769) and Wallachia (Bucharest, 17 November 1769); at Küçük Kaynarca (21 July 1774) it returned the principalities and became protector of Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788-1791)
wars.outcome: Wallachia was occupied by the Habsburgs in 1789 and given back: by the Treaty of Sistova (4 August 1791) 'Austria returned all the territory from its conquests save the small town of Orsova', which is not in Wallachia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Russian occupation of both principalities; the Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) returned all occupied lands except Bessarabia, the eastern half of Moldavia.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) set the Wallachian border on the Danube thalweg, gave Wallachia the rayas of Turnu, Giurgiu and Brăila and allowed Russia to occupy the principalities until an indemnity was paid.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Hungary and Transylvania along the Carpathians, with the Golden Horde and Moldavia in the east and the Danube forts are approximate; no treaty line is dated before 1718.
The Passarowitz treaty cut off Oltenia as a Habsburg province, a line agreed by treaty.
Most of the Ottoman frontier is the Danube with Ottoman rayas on the Wallachian bank; the Moldavian boundary is not dated on the pages opened.
The Treaty of Adrianople 'fixed the border between the Ottoman Empire and Wallachia on the thalweg of the Danube'.
